chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, both together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the upper arm when it is struck, so the wrist breaks from it. He said: If the palm dries up from it, so the fingers of the palm are all paralysed, then in it is two-thirds of the wergild of the hand. He said: And if some of the fingers are paralysed and some remain, then in each paralysed finger is two-thirds of its wergild. He said: And the same is the ruling regarding the leg and the foot when the toes of the foot are paralysed.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for compensation when fingers or toes are paralysed due to injury?
ai.summary: Transmitted through the reliable chain of al-Kulayni’s *al-Kafi*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides precise jurisprudential criteria for *diyah* (blood money) based on functional loss rather than mere anatomical injury. It establishes a standardized legal precedent in Shia fiqh where complete paralysis (*shall*) of the hand or foot fingers constitutes two-thirds of the limb's value, while partial paralysis is calculated proportionally, reflecting the principle of compensating for the loss of utility.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, both together from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali Bin Raib, from Al Fuzayl Bin Yasaar who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the upper-arms when it is hit, so the wrist breaks from it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the palm is dried up from it, so the fingers of the palm are paralysed, all of them, so regarding it is two-thirds of the wergild of the hand. And if some of the fingers are paralysed, and some remain (healthy), so with regards to each of the paralysed finger is two-thirds of its wergild. And like that is the judgement regarding the leg, and the feet, when the toes of the feet are paralysed’.
